It has been a number of years since my parents' passing.

3 years for my mother and nearly 5 years for my father.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Photos or videos, their sayings as well as how they handled certain situations are all reminders of how they viewed this life and how I should face current and future challenges

Koreans, long ago, physically remembered one's parents by performing a ritual that symbolically paid back parents sacrifice and devotion during first 3 years.

This was tending to and performing rituals for 2 actual years or 3 counting years.

By the time I was aware of my surroundings, that practice was largely displaced by men and women wearing a small emblem, a bow on their hair or on their lapel.

As a Christian, with cultural heritage rooted in old Korea as well as Old China, how do I remember and honor my parents.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Photos, videos, and remembered sayings of my parents—these are more than just nostalgia.

They are the blueprints for how my parents viewed and lived life and, by extension, how I should face my own challenges.

Long ago, Koreans physically manifested this gratitude through *Simyosari*, a three-year vigil at a parent's gravesite to symbolically repay the devotion received in infancy.

By the time I was old enough to notice, that tradition had shrunk to a simple tan bow on a lapel or in hair.

As a Christian with heritage rooted in the ancient traditions of Korea and China, I find myself asking:

> How do I honor them today?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Recounting their memories.

I have this summary.

They fulfilled the first and essential commandment found in OT.

> And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth...

They brought us into the world when the per capita GDP was 100 USD.

Secondly, they protected us from evil influences and nurtured us until we can decide and fend for ourselves. Mainly through home education, church attendance and then public education.

Among other attributes, I recall these

-   Independence

-   Frugal

-   Industry

-   Optimism

-   Sacrifice

------------------------------------------------------------------------

I visit their grave site regularly.

"Ultimately, I have come to realize that honoring my parents doesn't require a three-year vigil in a mountainside hut, nor is it fully captured by the small black bow I saw on the lapels of my youth.

As a Christian, I see my Korean heritage of **Hyo (Filial Piety)** not as a debt to the dead, but as a stewardship of the living.

\[To honor them is to 'give weight' to the faith they practiced and the resilience they forged when the world offered them nothing but \$100 a year and the scars of war. \]

By carrying their lessons into my own challenges—choosing hope over scarcity and protection over compromise—I am building a monument that won't weather away.

My life is the 'living scroll' where their legacy is written, and my gratitude is the quiet ritual I perform every day I walk in the values they gave me."
